event: VXE 528 in fixed wing loiter would not descend below 600 ft AGL when 400 ft was commanded, drifted off the orbit, and later stayed high on recovery before transitioning to VTOL at about 500 ft AGL.
failure_mode: aircraft kept climbing with throttle at zero in rising air, so it could not hold the lower commanded altitude
contributing: local AWOS gusts of 18 kt, Colorado Springs peak winds 37 kt
GCS altitude carrot reported not moving off 600 ft (not explained)

evidence.quote: Looks like a case of glider doing glider things. Throttle zero, and still climbing.
Local AWOS reporting wind shift w/ gusts of 18kt 1hr prior to launch. Suggesting winds extremely variable in the area.
Colorado springs (10nm away) reporting peak winds of 37kt in same time period

would_settle_it.what: throttle and altitude trace confirming climb at zero throttle
commanded altitude received by the AP versus the 600 ft carrot shown on the GCS

reasoning: An engineer's plot showed the aircraft climbing with throttle at zero, and nearby weather stations reported strong, variable winds. This supports rising air holding the aircraft above the commanded altitude. It does not explain the report that the commanded altitude carrot itself would not move off 600 ft.
notes: The carrot not moving off 600 ft AGL suggests a command acceptance or display question that the ticket never addresses. Canceled and closed as environmental.

event: VXE 528 aborted its VTOL launch about 10 ft off the ground and landed because the autopilot judged the launch altitude request too high.
component: Jennings GCS launch altitude request with autopilot launch altitude limit check
failure_mode: slightly negative ground AGL (-1 to -5 ft, factory DTED) was added to the 300 ft launch altitude, giving a 333 ft request that exceeded the 331 ft autopilot limit, so launch aborted
contributing: launch altitude set to exactly 300 ft, at the limit
factory DTED loaded on the GCS

evidence.quote: [21:27:10.274 1737.275] DebugMsg Altitude request too high, launch aborted
The threshold was 331 feet but the request was for 333.
When you’re right up against the limit there is a small chance of this happening based on the vehicle being at a “negative” AGL altitude during launch.
@Alexander Alan Arnold No change has been made to Jennings GCS, I believe the issue could still occur but is unlikely.

team_root_cause:
he Jennings GCS was loaded with factory DTED and the launch altitude was specified as 300 ft exactly.  This issue appears to have the same symptoms as the but in MCM, namely a slightly negative reported AGL on the ground is additive to the launch altitude goal, which exceeds the climb limit + margin in the autopilot.  In this case, the reported altitude was -1 to -5 feet:
 
[embedded: slightly-negative-agl (51204c15-c816-420b-9b18-60c3600cc775).png]
reasoning: The debug log names the abort: altitude request 333 ft against a 331 ft threshold. Engineers traced the extra height to a slightly negative reported AGL on the ground being added to the 300 ft launch goal. The abort itself worked as designed; the fault is the altitude request logic with launch altitude at the limit.
notes: Designed abort triggered by a degraded input (negative ground AGL). VXEP-1982 (VXE 897, same error) is a related recurrence, not read. No AN was issued.

event: VXE 592 in a 700 ft AGL fixed wing orbit rolled hard right, inverted, dove and crashed, destroying the aircraft.
failure_mode: fixed wing attitude and rate bias estimate jumped 30+ degrees in one time step, likely from a single out of range (probably magnetometer) measurement; FWAP believed it was pitching up and pitched down hard into an overspeed dive
contributing: no clipping of single erroneous sensor measurements in AHRS
XCOMM logs dropped out before the event, removing raw rate data
E140 gimbal flipping mode enabled (EO/IR switch just before)
IMU or mag sensor failure not ruled out

evidence.quote: Fixed-wing believes it is pitching up and only rolling slightly, which explains why the autopilot responds by pitching down hard.
Accel and rate changes did not look all that similar, while mag data did.
an out-of-range measurement resulted in corruption of the
3. Investigation inconclusive on true root cause
6/20/2025 - smisek - tested elevator booster board using electronics checkout, checked okay.
[10:44:53.876] Fixed-wing ignoring VTOL Mag

team_root_cause: See PPT linked above.  Best guess is a software glitch corrupting the AHRS, but cannot rule out sensor failure.

would_settle_it.what: full rate, mag and bias plots at the jump
raw VTOL mag values sent to the FWAP at the time of the jump
any raw IMU data before the 2574.58 dropout

reasoning: The investigation report shows the FWAP attitude estimate disagreed with the VTOL estimate and with the flight path, and jumped in one step, so the FWAP pitched down into the ground. Elevator and boost board tested good, airspeed and GPS were consistent, and a sim injection of bad mag data reproduced the bias step. The report itself calls the true root cause inconclusive, and sensor failure cannot be excluded, so this is narrowed to the FWAP AHRS handling of an erroneous measurement.
notes: The two customer report PDFs are identical. RMA-704 found a bird strike unlikely; RMA-705 is gimbal crash damage. RMA-704 06192025.pdf and RMA-705 EPS6170 pdf are scans with no text. Earlier 592 incident VXEP-453 not read (ticket says no evidence it is related).

evidence.quote: We should explore a heat related failure of the ESCs, Battery Failure, Connector Failure, U11 on XCOMM, or any other systemic issue that can bring down the CW systems.

component: D750 fuel cell power or grounding (suspected) affecting XCOMM network switch

contributing: outside air temperature 80 to 90 F
